corrections: Reader-domain clarification: interior stationary fraction requires positive separately conserved two-sector densities, -1<w_other<1/2 and finite positive y; it establishes no peak existence, maximum, value or location.

Reader locator clarification: #p9.m9 is the fraction definition; #p9.m30 is phi_i in the n2 sound-speed statement. Original packet and contract predecessor are preserved; neither clarification is a printed-source correction.
limitations: Omega_phi(a) cannot be substituted for the instantaneous total-density fraction. A constant density-normalizer interpretation and any Omega_phi,0-to-X_c conversion are conditional reader conventions until the original implementation fixes their ownership.

For separately conserved positive scalar and aggregate non-scalar densities, 0<F<1 and a common pressure/density convention, an interior stationary fraction requires w_phi=w_other. With w_total=F w_phi+(1-F)w_other, this is equivalent to w_total=w_phi only on that positive two-sector decomposition. For n=3 the conditional relation is y=(a_stat/a_c)^(9/2)=(1+w_other(a_stat))/(1/2-w_other(a_stat)), requiring -1<w_other(a_stat)<1/2 and finite positive y. The denominator vanishes at w_other=1/2; w_other=-1 gives no finite positive y. The relation is implicit for a varying background and does not establish a maximum, a unique peak or a numerical peak fraction; boundaries and a derivative sign change must also be checked.

The cosine argument varphi/f requires compatible units, but the selected letter does not specify physical units or the normalization/domain of sampled phi_i. No field value, angle range or prior bound is inferred from fitted summaries. Early dot varphi_i=0 is a source assumption, not a supplied full initial-mode prescription.

The explicit MontePython footnote URL and CLASS bibliography are navigation witnesses, not an EDE repository/commit/configuration. Original code identity is unresolved within the retained sources, rather than proved globally unavailable.
